original_idea.body:
# Follow-Up to Finding>>Exploiting Asymmetry: Does the Asymmetry Hold Under Iterative AI Prompting?

**Problem:** The Mozilla finding showed only 2/22 exploits generated in a single-pass attempt ($4000 API spend). It is unknown whether iterative, multi-turn exploit refinement narrows the asymmetry.

**Direction:** Take 5 known simple vulnerabilities (publicly disclosed with PoC). Attempt exploit generation with a fixed LLM under three conditions: (a) single-turn, (b) 3-turn iterative refinement, (c) 10-turn with feedback. Measure exploit success rate per condition. Assess whether the asymmetry narrows under iterative prompting.

**Why it matters:** If iterative prompting closes the finding>>exploiting gap, current safety assumptions based on single-pass exploit failure may be too optimistic.

**Relevant context:** Mozilla + Anthropic 2026: 2/22 exploits, single-pass. OpenAI Aardvark: multi-step agentic approach. The effect of iterative refinement on exploit generation is not characterized in the literature.
